verses.1: When the sages spoke thus, Rama replied, "O sages, tell me what the task is; first of all, let your fear depart."
verses.2: When Rama spoke thus, Bhargava (Chyavana) replied, "O King, listen to the origin of our fears and of this region."
verses.3: O King, formerly in the Krita Yuga, there was an exceedingly powerful Daitya, the eldest son of Lola, named Madhu, who was a great demon.
verses.4: He was devoted to Brahmins, a protector, and firmly resolved in his wisdom, and he had an unequalled affection for the exceedingly generous gods.
verses.5: That Madhu, endowed with great valor and steadfast in righteousness, performed penance for many thousands of years to please Rudra.
verses.6: Rudra became pleased with him and went to grant a boon, and with great respect, an extraordinary boon was given to him by Rudra.
verses.7: The great-souled Rudra, very pleased, extracted a trident of great power and splendor from his own trident, gave it, and indeed spoke these words.
verses.8: “This unequalled act of righteousness, which pleases me, has been performed by you; filled with supreme affection, I give you this excellent weapon.”
verses.9: O great Asura, as long as you do not contend with gods and Brahmins, this spear shall remain yours; otherwise, it will meet its destruction.
verses.10: Whoever fearlessly challenges you to battle, the spear will reduce him to ashes and then return to your hand.
verses.11: Having thus obtained a boon from Rudra, the great Asura bowed down to the great god and spoke these words again.
verses.12: O Lord, may this excellent spear always remain with my lineage, for you are indeed the lord of the gods.
verses.13: To Madhu, who was speaking thus, the greatly effulgent god Shiva, the lord of all beings, replied, "This will not be so."
verses.14: May your auspicious words, granted by my grace, not be in vain; indeed, only one of your sons will possess this trident.
verses.15: As long as this trident remains in your son's hand, he will be invincible to all beings, being one who wields the trident.
verses.16: Thus, having obtained this very great and wonderful boon from the god, Madhu, the best of demons, caused a splendid city to be built.
verses.17: His beloved and highly fortunate wife was Kumbhinasi, who was indeed the very radiant daughter of Vishvavasu by Anala.
verses.18: Her son was the very powerful and terrible Lavana, who, being evil-minded, committed only sinful deeds from his childhood onwards.
verses.19: Seeing his ill-behaved son, Madhu was filled with anger and sorrow, yet he did not say anything to him.
verses.20: Madhu, having left this world, entered the abode of Varuna, and after placing the trident with Lavana, he offered a boon to him.
verses.21: Lavana, by the power of the trident and his own wickedness, torments the three worlds, especially the ascetics.
verses.22: Having heard of Lavana's power and the nature of his trident, O Rama, you are our ultimate refuge and authority.
verses.23: O Rama, many kings were formerly implored for protection by fear-stricken sages, but we do not know of any true protector.
verses.24: Having heard that Ravana, along with his army and vehicles, has been killed, we know no other king on earth as a protector, and therefore, O dear one, we wish for you to protect those afflicted by fear from Lavana.
verses.25: O Rama of undiminished valor, you are capable of removing this cause of fear that has arisen and been reported, so please fulfill that wish. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 61 ।। Thus ends the sixty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
